hypothesis: The recorded range-classification AVX2 candidate was valid but measured at 22.43 µs, while a paired-block candidate measured 17.93 µs. Replacing shift/mask-based bit assembly with AVX2 pairwise multiply-add packing and lane interleaving may reduce packing work; classification overhead, stores, or tails could erase any gain. This candidate keeps bounded full-block accesses and uses scalar decoding when its vector or safe-quartet paths cannot accept the input.
notes: Only src/candidate.cpp is changed in this proposal. AVX2 code is isolated with a GCC/Clang target attribute and guarded by runtime CPU feature detection; no build flags or thread settings are changed. The supplied facts identify AMD EPYC 9654 and GCC 14.2, but no local commands, correctness checks, frozen-build verification, Lena test, or timing were performed here. The controller must compile and validate empty/short strings, vector-boundary lengths, padding cases, random valid inputs, and Lena before reporting performance.
transformations: Retained the original scalar decoder under an internal reference name to preserve fallback behavior for malformed inputs.
Added an AVX2-targeted full-block decoder with vector range masks and arithmetic offsets for the Base64 alphabet; invalid vector blocks fall back to the reference path.

Replaced per-output-bit assembly with AVX2 pairwise multiply-add packing, saturating pack operations, and lane-local byte interleaving; loads are bounded to 32 input bytes and exactly 24 output bytes are copied per block.

Decoded the residual input in bounded four-character quartets, preserving terminal padding while avoiding wide scalar stores on valid short inputs and tails; unrecognized input falls back to the original decoder.
